title: Re-entrant Transaction Loops Across Boundaries
pattern: An active transaction context calling a boundary service which in turn re-enters the transaction scope or invokes a parallel transaction on the same database.
why_bad: It causes database lock contentions, deadlocks, and transaction isolation failures. It also breaks aggregate consistency boundary invariants.
detection: Nested transactional blocks (e.g., `#[transactional]` attributes) on methods that invoke each other transitively within the same execution path.
counterexample: Explicit, independent database connections managed by a coordinator pool. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Separate transactional persistence calls from in-memory aggregate behavior. Batch updates and run db flushes at the absolute end of the application use case.
source: *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* by Martin Fowler (p. 291, "Re-entrant behavior problems").
